Roll the highlight reel! Here’s what you missed at
UiPath
FUSION:

The one I think you should check out is UiPath Cartographer. It provides a living, governed view of how an enterprise process actually runs. Cartographer accelerates capturing the operational knowledge required for process orchestration and automation by analyzing process documentation, architecture diagrams, meeting transcriptions, and more. Now, tribal knowledge becomes actionable.

This is the first step in UiPath's 4-step "Map of Work," which spans capture, build, run, and learn. With Cartographer's process design document and spec in hand, UiPath for Coding Agents can then get to work and develop the bot or agent. IT teams then add the agents to the respective process to (ideally) orchestrate it end-to-end. And because drift between the spec and the reality on the ground naturally occurs, a decision ledger is the fourth step, which closes the loop of keeping information current, relevant, and actionable, before Cartographer takes action again.

Could this be the answer to: "Do you know how your process actually runs?"


PS: This is just one of the product launches. Don't forget to check them all...

I’ve been to Las Vegas at least 15 times, but this trip felt incredibly special. Here’s why.

𝟭. 𝗜 𝗱𝗶𝗱𝗻’𝘁 𝗳𝗲𝗲𝗹 𝗹𝗶𝗸𝗲 𝗮𝗻 𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗲. 𝗜 𝗳𝗲𝗹𝘁 𝗽𝗮𝗿𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻.

UiPath FUSION brought together over 2,000 people, which created a very different experience from the massive conferences.
You could actually ask questions during panels, join smaller discussions, and share feedback directly with product teams.

It was also great to hear customers describe the better-together story firsthand: Databricks powering the data layer, and UiPath orchestrating how that work gets executed across the enterprise.

I didn’t just listen. I got to participate.

𝟮. 𝗜 𝗰𝗮𝗺𝗲 𝗲𝘅𝗽𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗔𝗜. 𝗜 𝗹𝗲𝗳𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗮𝗯𝗼𝘂𝘁 𝗵𝘂𝗺𝗮𝗻 𝗰𝗼𝗹𝗹𝗮𝗯𝗼𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻.

I thought conversations to be about how much more work we can automate with AI agents. Instead, I heard more about how humans, agents, and automation can work better together.

And the announcements reflected that.
The new Map of Work gives AI the enterprise context. UiPath Cartographer helps capture how work really happens, including processes, rules, exceptions, systems, and human judgment. And Process Atlas provides curated starting points for common enterprise processes.

The goal is to give AI enough context to be useful while keeping people responsible for the decisions that matter.

𝟯. 𝗘𝘃𝗲𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗯𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗮𝗻𝗮𝗹𝘆𝘀𝘁 𝗿𝗼𝗹𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗶𝗻𝗴.

I found this most interesting. Instead of spending so much time chasing stakeholders and writing process documentation from scratch, Cartographer can draft the process map and specifications.

The human becomes the person who validates it, resolves contradictions, and ultimately decides what is true.

𝟰. 𝗔𝗻𝗱 𝗳𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗹𝗹𝘆, 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗲𝗼𝗽𝗹𝗲.

Everyone I met was incredibly approachable and kind. From product teams who genuinely wanted feedback to leaders willing to sit down and have thoughtful conversations, there was very little ego in the room.

Then I learned that one of UiPath’s core values is literally 𝘏𝘶𝘮𝘣𝘭𝘦.

𝘒𝘦𝘦𝘱 𝘢𝘯 𝘰𝘱𝘦𝘯 𝘮𝘪𝘯𝘥. 𝘊𝘶𝘭𝘵𝘪𝘷𝘢𝘵𝘦 𝘬𝘪𝘯𝘥𝘯𝘦𝘴𝘴. 𝘉𝘦 𝘢 𝘵𝘦𝘢𝘮 𝘱𝘭𝘢𝘺𝘦𝘳. 𝘊𝘩𝘦𝘤𝘬 𝘺𝘰𝘶𝘳 𝘦𝘨𝘰.

Thank you,
UiPath
, for an incredibly thoughtful few days at FUSION ❤️

What does it take to trust AI with the work that matters?
That was the question on my mind as
Daniel Dines
opened
UiPath
FUSION.

It is my first Fusion, and after a decade of working with clients on RPA, the progress on display is striking.

As Daniel put it: “AI doesn’t create business value on its own. That’s what business orchestration was built for. It gives AI context, coordination, and the governance the enterprise demands.”

That distinction matters.

The enterprise challenge goes beyond deploying more AI. It requires an operating model that gives AI the context to understand work, the guardrails to act within clear boundaries, and the governance to improve outcomes without compromising oversight.
UiPath
’s announcements pointed to what that can look like in practice:
✅ UiPath Cartographer
introduces a living Map of Work; a continuously updated view of how work gets done. It brings together process knowledge, business rules, exceptions, human context, tribal knowledge, or expensive consulting engagements. It is designed to propose changes while accountable process owners retain approval authority. That is the kind of context AI needs to move beyond pilots and into trusted execution.
✅ Platform updates
extend enterprise-grade governance across models, data, integrations, identities, and agent behavior. Model Hub provides visibility into model use; Runtime Checker validates agent behavior against policies while agents are running; and Data Fabric helps ground agents in governed, current business data. Governance is becoming part of the architecture.
✅ UiPath Test Cloud
advances the idea of a “dark testing factory,” where autonomous testing takes on routine quality work and people focus on judgment, risk, and exceptions. As coding agents accelerate software creation, testing cannot remain a manual bottleneck. It becomes essential infrastructure for responsible speed.
✅ The Global Partner Awards
reinforce that transformation does not scale through technology alone. It scales through an ecosystem that can bring orchestration into industries, operating models, and real business outcomes.

My takeaway is that we are moving from disconnected AI tools to coordinated, end-to-end
business orchestration
, with context, controls, and accountability built in from the start.

That is how enterprises can begin to trust AI with work that matters.

What surprised you most within the first 90 days on your process orchestration journey? “By using a process map, we could have a common conversation with the business,” shared
Maxim Ioffe
, Senior Director Global Intelligent Automation at Wesco.

This process map allowed the team to compare the documented process state to what’s actually happening in operations. This created a common starting point for the conversation with the business and shift it from automating tasks to automating process end-to-end.

Maxim highlighted the need for a holistic view of the process steps and the systems it is orchestrated across. Customer care, sales, and operations processes can benefit most from additional automation. 

He’s not alone on this journey. Other leaders on the customer panel shared how they have automated generating 3 million certificate of insurance per year or handling over 12,000 airline crew travel reservations per year to drive real impact.

Now, it’s up to leaders to turn it into action. The five pieces of advice from the panel:
- Don’t use AI like a hammer
- Enable the business to change their process
- Develop the governance framework upfront
- Step back and automate processes E2E
- Reduce the task item backlog

What would you add?


PS: Maxim and I have known each other for a few years and created some content together. This time, we finally got to meet IRL at
UiPath
FUSION.
